title: Pulse Beam Factory Digital Twin — Truthful Physicalization
page0: Turn the software manufacturing system into a beautiful explorable fake physical machine. The building may be richly architectural and decorated, but the physical machine representation must accurately reflect the real software state for humans. Every machine, line, light, queue, receipt, breakdown and maintenance condition must derive from real software evidence rather than decorative storytelling.
correctedQuestion: What spatial language and data-binding model lets a human walk through MOOR's software factory and understand real production state at a glance, while keeping decoration free, authority external, and every operational object traceable to software evidence?
objective: Make invisible software manufacturing legible through a premium 3D digital twin that never confuses visual metaphor with implementation truth.

knownEvidence.claim: The Citadel already renders graph-driven laser architecture and explorable space.
Subsystem truth is modeled across documented/implemented/wired/verified/receipt-backed/visualized dimensions.
Manufacturing roles for Objective, HUB, Funnel, Assembly, Harness, Verifier, Refinery, Learning and Beam are mapped.
Cumulative verified machinery and supersession lineage can be represented as a factory graph.
FactoryTwinSnapshot now deterministically composes maintenance truth, cumulative machinery, Funnel topology, real work orders, receipts, metrics and semantic spatial bindings.
Build/change work has a real WorkOrder/Traveler/QC/NCR/rework/release ledger and plant snapshot.
Snapshot identity, evidence requirements, WIP bindings, supersession and receipt tracing are executable regression checks.

openQuestions: Which software states are important enough to deserve persistent physical objects rather than temporary overlays?
What spatial grouping makes production routing understandable without copying software module boundaries too literally?
Which status distinctions can be understood pre-attentively through motion, line continuity, occupancy, material state or light without relying only on color?
How should a human distinguish authority state from health state from work-in-progress state?
How much historical machinery should remain physically visible before the space becomes unreadable?
When a machine is superseded, should its physical representation move to archive space, ghost in place, or remain discoverable only through inspection?
What should physically happen when a work order blocks, fails verification, enters rework or exhausts budget?
Which metrics deserve ambient representation and which require explicit inspection?
How should mobile navigation preserve the same mental model when the whole factory cannot fit in view?
Which parts of the building should be stable architecture versus procedurally regenerated from machine inventory?
What fidelity tier can phone hardware sustain while keeping the same semantic layout as desktop?
What is the minimum useful non-3D fallback for accessibility and debugging?
assumptions: The physical representation is an HMI/digital twin, not a simulation that creates truth.
The building architecture can be expressive as long as operational glyphs remain data-bound.
Existing graph and maintenance data remain primary inputs.
nonGoals: Do not represent every source file as a physical object.
Do not animate fake work to make the room feel busy.
Do not derive health from whether a visual object rendered successfully.
Do not require 3D interaction to operate production-critical actions.

districts.physical: modular bays that appear only for real active or registered cells
quiet archive mezzanine reachable by inspection

semanticLayers.rule: Must map to real subsystem/capability IDs.
May request actions but cannot self-authorize them.
Remains in Funnel/receipt systems outside the renderer.

visualSemantics.healthyVerified: continuous stable beam + clear identifier; never inferred without evidence
visualSemantics.candidate: white/ice provisional beam with explicit CANDIDATE text
visualSemantics.degraded: broken/pulsed route with exact reason inspectable
visualSemantics.gap: red crossed datum / missing segment; never hidden by decoration
visualSemantics.blockedWork: stationary packet at real blocking station
visualSemantics.rework: reverse or side-loop routing with NCR reference
visualSemantics.superseded: dim archive representation with visible supersession link
visualSemantics.unknown: neutral unlit state labeled UNKNOWN, not green

proceduralGeometry.principle: Store semantic anchors, seed, generator version and recipe instead of baking every decorative point.

failureModes.containment: Snapshot shows generated timestamp/source hashes and explicit stale state.
Renderer never exposes a direct promote/verify mutation; controls call real authority interfaces.
Semantic priority, districting and default hiding of archive/detail layers.
Same entity IDs/routes with lower decorative density, not a different information model.

maintenanceModel.sourceOfTruth: FactoryTwinSnapshot from factory-twin-core.js, composed from canonical maintenance JSON, Capability Memory factory graph, software plant ledger and Funnel graph.
maintenanceModel.verification: Snapshot contract test + visual semantic regression + entity binding checks.
maintenanceModel.driftDetection: Any displayed authoritative entity without a valid source binding fails CI.
maintenanceModel.maintenanceBurden: Decorative generators may evolve independently; semantic binding schema remains versioned.

observability.glance: Active authority, candidate authority, line health, blocked/rework work and known maintenance gaps.
observability.inspect: Files, tests, receipts, owner layer, capability lineage and last verification.
observability.trace: Select a work order to light its exact route through planning, cells, QC and release.

securityAuthority.rule: The twin is read-mostly observability plus request controls; it cannot mint authority receipts or mutate production law.
securityAuthority.sensitiveAction: Any action leaving the twin routes through MOOR.request/Funnel.

acceptance: Every authoritative-looking machine in 3D maps to a real machine-readable entity.
Every health state maps to evidence or an explicit unknown/gap.
The same software state yields the same semantic layout regardless of decorative seed.
Work orders can be traced end-to-end through real stations.
Superseded machinery remains inspectable without polluting the default floor.
Mobile and desktop preserve the same semantics.
rollback: Keep current Citadel renderer as a compatible projection until snapshot-driven bindings pass; new twin layers are additive and can be disabled independently.
